facts.text: Clay earned its name from 19th‑century statesman Henry Clay, honoring the famed American attorney and statesman.
In 1827, Clay split from the original Cicero township, becoming one of the first towns carved out of the Central New York Military Tract.
The town’s first school, a simple log building, opened at Clay Corners around 1808, marking the start of formal education in the area.
Micron Technology announced a $100 billion investment in 2022 to build a giant semiconductor complex at White Pine Commerce Park in Clay.
A renovated stretch of the Erie Canal winds along Clay’s borders, following the Oneida and Seneca rivers before they merge into the Oswego River.
Clay’s northern edge hugs the Oneida River, while the Seneca River defines its western boundary; the two rivers meet near the community of Three Rivers.
